clean_source_blocks.text: Teenager Mirra Andreeva fulfills her huge potential with a first Grand Slam title as Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska is denied a fairytale French Open victory.

Mirra Andreeva is the first teenager to win the Roland Garros women's singles title since Iga Swiatek in 2020 Teenager Mirra Andreeva won her first Grand Slam title as Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska was denied a fairytale French Open victory. Andreeva, 19, fulfilled the potential she has long shown with a 6-3 6-2 victory over an opponent who was a 500-1 outsider before the tournament. Russian eighth seed Andreeva is the youngest woman to win the Roland Garros title since Monica Seles in 1992. After securing victory in one hour and 22 minutes, Andreeva fell to the court in elation before quickly running up to the stands for a warm embrace with her coach Conchita Martinez - herself a former major champion after winning Wimbledon in 1994.

Chwalinska was the second qualifier to reach a Grand Slam singles final in the Open era - after Britain's Emma Raducanu Expectation has followed Andreeva ever since her WTA Tour breakthrough at the 2023 Madrid Open, where her talent and fearlessness led to praise from Britain's former world number one Andy Murray. It felt like a matter of time until she won one of the sport's biggest prizes, but developing your game and dealing with the hype under intense scrutiny can take time. Andreeva, who was born in Siberia and trained in France, reached the French Open semi-finals in 2024 and has continued to improve under the tutelage of Martinez. She thanked Martinez in her on-court speech for "sharing her experiences and giving me so much advice" over the two years they have worked together.

"I've been watching Roland Garros since I was very young and it has always been a dream to win this trophy," Andreeva said. Andreeva overcame a tense start, where nerves and a swirling wind led to the final starting with four successive breaks of serve. It was world number 114 Chwalinska who held first - much to the delight of the 15,000-strong crowd who gave her vociferous support throughout. Despite thousands of Polish fans cheering Chwalinska on, Andreeva showed her increased maturity to maintain composure and reel off the next nine games to take a 6-3 5-0 lead. There was more tension when Andreeva was unable to serve out victory at the first attempt, but she recovered to take her first championship point on Chwalinska's serve with a backhand winner.

payload.title: Mirra Andreeva voitti Ranskan avoimet ja ensimmäisen Grand Slam -tittelinsä
payload.summary: 19-vuotias Mirra Andreeva kukisti Maja Chwalinskan Ranskan avointen finaalissa 6–3, 6–2 ja nousi Roland Garrosin nuorimmaksi naisten mestariksi sitten vuoden 1992.
payload.content:
Mirra Andreeva on voittanut uransa ensimmäisen Grand Slam -mestaruuden Ranskan avoimissa. Venäläinen kahdeksanneksi sijoitettu 19-vuotias kukisti puolalaisen karsijan Maja Chwalinskan finaalissa 6–3, 6–2. Chwalinskan yllättävä matka päättyi finaalitappioon, kun Andreeva ratkaisi ottelun tunnissa ja 22 minuutissa.

## Nuori mestari Roland Garrosilla

Andreevasta tuli ensimmäinen teini-ikäinen Roland Garrosin naisten kaksinpelin mestari sitten Iga Swiatekin vuoden 2020 voiton. Hän on myös nuorin naispelaaja, joka on voittanut Ranskan avointen mestaruuden sitten Monica Selesin vuoden 1992.

Voiton jälkeen Andreeva kaatui kentälle riemuitsemaan ja nousi pian katsomoon halaamaan valmentajaansa Conchita Martinezia. Martinez on itse entinen Grand Slam -voittaja, sillä hän voitti Wimbledonin vuonna 1994.

Andreevaa on pidetty yhtenä tenniksen lupaavimmista nuorista pelaajista siitä lähtien, kun hän teki läpimurtonsa WTA-kiertueella Madridissa vuonna 2023. Hän eteni Ranskan avoimissa välieriin jo vuonna 2024 ja on jatkanut kehittymistään Martinezin johdolla. Andreeva kiitti kenttäpuheessaan valmentajaansa kokemusten jakamisesta ja neuvoista heidän kahden vuoden yhteistyönsä aikana.

## Chwalinskan yllätys jäi vajaaksi

Chwalinska oli vasta toinen karsintojen kautta Grand Slam -kaksinpelin finaaliin edennyt pelaaja avoimella aikakaudella. Ennen turnausta hänen mestaruutensa nähtiin erittäin epätodennäköisenä, mutta maailmanlistan sijalta 114 lähtenyt puolalainen sai Pariisissa vahvan kannatuksen.

Finaali alkoi hermostuneesti. Tuuli ja paine näkyivät pelissä, ja ottelun neljä ensimmäistä syöttövuoroa päättyivät murtoihin. Chwalinska piti syöttönsä ensimmäisenä, mikä innosti noin 15 000 katsojan yleisöä.

Andreeva kuitenkin rauhoitti pelinsä ja voitti sen jälkeen yhdeksän peräkkäistä peliä nousten 6–3, 5–0 -johtoon. Hän ei saanut ottelua päätökseen ensimmäisellä yrityksellään omassa syöttövuorossaan, mutta ratkaisi mestaruuden Chwalinskan syötössä ensimmäisellä ottelupallollaan rystylyönnillä.

Andreeva sanoi katsoneensa Roland Garrosia lapsesta asti ja pitäneensä pokaalin voittamista unelmanaan.

Chwalinska oli vasta toinen karsija avoimella aikakaudella Grand Slam -kaksinpelin finaalissa.
article.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu packetin lähdetietoihin; julkisessa tekstissä ei ole lähdemerkintöjä eikä lisättyjä taustafaktoja.
article.source_text:
Teenager Mirra Andreeva fulfills her huge potential with a first Grand Slam title as Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska is denied a fairytale French Open victory.

Mirra Andreeva is the first teenager to win the Roland Garros women's singles title since Iga Swiatek in 2020 Teenager Mirra Andreeva won her first Grand Slam title as Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska was denied a fairytale French Open victory. Andreeva, 19, fulfilled the potential she has long shown with a 6-3 6-2 victory over an opponent who was a 500-1 outsider before the tournament. Russian eighth seed Andreeva is the youngest woman to win the Roland Garros title since Monica Seles in 1992. After securing victory in one hour and 22 minutes, Andreeva fell to the court in elation before quickly running up to the stands for a warm embrace with her coach Conchita Martinez - herself a former major champion after winning Wimbledon in 1994.

Chwalinska was the second qualifier to reach a Grand Slam singles final in the Open era - after Britain's Emma Raducanu Expectation has followed Andreeva ever since her WTA Tour breakthrough at the 2023 Madrid Open, where her talent and fearlessness led to praise from Britain's former world number one Andy Murray. It felt like a matter of time until she won one of the sport's biggest prizes, but developing your game and dealing with the hype under intense scrutiny can take time. Andreeva, who was born in Siberia and trained in France, reached the French Open semi-finals in 2024 and has continued to improve under the tutelage of Martinez. She thanked Martinez in her on-court speech for "sharing her experiences and giving me so much advice" over the two years they have worked together.

"I've been watching Roland Garros since I was very young and it has always been a dream to win this trophy," Andreeva said. Andreeva overcame a tense start, where nerves and a swirling wind led to the final starting with four successive breaks of serve. It was world number 114 Chwalinska who held first - much to the delight of the 15,000-strong crowd who gave her vociferous support throughout. Despite thousands of Polish fans cheering Chwalinska on, Andreeva showed her increased maturity to maintain composure and reel off the next nine games to take a 6-3 5-0 lead. There was more tension when Andreeva was unable to serve out victory at the first attempt, but she recovered to take her first championship point on Chwalinska's serve with a backhand winner.
